events.title: Iran Iraqi Kurdistan post-referendum border suspension
events.scope: Three official Iran–Iraqi Kurdistan crossings with distinct reopening phases.
events.crossings: Parwezkhan and Haji Omaran, reopened January 2 2018; Bashmakh, reopened October 25 2017.
events.exceptions: People already waiting were initially allowed through; semi-official Tawqela remained open.
events.enforcement: Not independently established
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no current-status inference
events.official_rationale: Response to Kurdish independence referendum and request by Iraqi federal government.
events.context: Closures accompanied measures to isolate the Kurdish region after its September 2017 referendum.
events.uncertainty: The main closure is dated October 15 by contemporary customs reporting; Iran initially denied new measures. Two gates reopened January 2 and Bashmakh October 25. Earlier drill and air measures are separate. Other reports' differing post counts remain a reporting disagreement.

historical.duration_note: 63–93 calendar days to the stated endpoint from reported date precision; not proof of continuous full closure

events.title: Turkey Iran COVID road-crossing restrictions
events.scope: Gürbulak / Bazargan and other land gates
events.crossings: Gürbulak / Bazargan and other land gates
events.direction: Iran to Türkiye initially; controlled outbound trade treated separately
events.movement: Passengers and ordinary road-vehicle movement; freight exceptions and substitute arrangements varied.
events.exceptions: Controlled exports and transit toward Iran continued initially; screened Turkish returns were permitted at Gürbulak. Rail wagons without personnel were permitted from March 4. On May 5 entry processing began for 280 waiting trucks under quarantine and health precautions; driver nationality was not specified.
events.enforcement: Official operational accounts support the freight arrangements; independent gate-by-gate observation is not established.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no current-status inference
events.official_rationale: Prevent COVID-19 spread.
events.context: Road restrictions operated alongside substitute rail and contact-free freight arrangements.
events.uncertainty: June 4 concerns general international freight restoration, not passenger reopening or the first permitted truck entry. A May 6 Trade Ministry notice identifies the May 5 exception as returning Turkish trucks already inside Iran before closure; newly arriving transit trucks were excluded. Driver nationality is not separately established. Rail substitution and screened returns preclude an all-traffic continuous interval; no matched continuous category is yet reconstructed.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Health minister and official ministry page describe Iran-to-Turkey road/rail suspension.
Contemporary Anadolu dates Sunday February 23 at 17:00; official page added February 24 describes statement without reliable independent event date.
June 4 trade minister announcement concerns freight; passenger end unproven.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): COVID spread in Iran explicitly cited.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the included ordinary-passenger restriction, with goods and emergency passages excepted. Contemporary reopening reporting supports the recorded scoped episode. The parent concerns the Algeria–Tunisia land frontier, both-way ordinary passengers/private cars. Nine posts are reported; AFP and Algerian Radio supply separate named-post observation, not an individual census of all posts. Retain 17 March 2020–15 July 2022, 850 calendar days, with qualified continuity and scope. AFP supplies retrospective exact onset; local resumption is observed. Calendar dates do not establish exact elapsed hours. Health and biosecurity / Human disease control is the reported pandemic purpose. No additional rationale is inferred from travel decline or reopening diplomacy. AFP reporting and Algerian Radio ministerial/local accounts were directly inspected. The minister’s 75-percent passenger reduction is consistent with exceptions, and rules out a zero-movement interpretation. The scoped phase remains unlocated. Named-post reporting does not itself approve a coordinate or whole-frontier operational geometry. Separate challenge: the goods-continuation statement is supported by a reported presidential account in Anadolu, rather than the inspected AFP passage. A June freight report describes border transshipment and later through-truck permission; no unrestricted or uniform freight-vehicle operation is inferred.

events.title: India excludes selected Bangladeshi imports from land ports
events.scope: May 17: garments barred at every land port; listed foods, drinks, cotton waste, plastic/PVC goods and furniture barred at named regional ports. June 27 and August 11 amendments added specified flax/jute fibres, yarns, fabrics, cordage and sacks/bags to all-land-port prohibitions.
events.crossings: All land ports for garments and later specified fibre/jute products; northeast states plus Changrabandha/Fulbari for other May-listed goods.
events.movement: Specified Bangladeshi garments and regional import categories from May 17; additional flax/jute fibre, yarn, fabric, cordage and sack/bag categories from June 27 and August 11.
events.exceptions: May notification exempts fish, LPG, edible oil, crushed stone and Bangladesh transit exports to Nepal/Bhutan. Named seaports remain permitted; June/August additions route through Nhava Sheva, with Nepal/Bhutan transit exempt but re-export into India prohibited.
events.imposing_authority: India Directorate General of Foreign Trade
events.enforcement: Published import-port eligibility rule; this record establishes prohibition, not measured compliance at each gate.
events.consequences: Permitted routing shifted to named seaports for garments; costs not quantified.
events.status_observation: Closure evidenced as of 2025-05-17; subsequent status unresolved

events.context: Notification regulates port eligibility for selected imports; motive not established in instrument.
events.uncertainty: Selective goods restriction, not all freight or people. June and August additions are within-regime scope changes. Gazette, reproductions and consolidated schedule are one documentary origin; no measured gate-level compliance or final repeal established.
